prompt: sha256sum --check printed OK for a downloaded binary. What does that prove?

choices.text: The binary has no known vulnerabilities
choices.why: A checksum knows nothing about the contents' quality.

choices.text: The file matches the published checksum
choices.why: Right. It says nothing about who published either.

choices.text: The publisher is who they claim to be
choices.why: The checksum came from the same place as the file.

choices.text: Nobody could have replaced the release
choices.why: Whoever replaced the binary could replace the checksum beside it.

prompt: Match each piece to what it does.

choices.text: One stored in a different registry
choices.why: The signature travels with the digest, not the registry.

choices.text: One downloaded over a slow link
choices.why: Speed does not change the bytes.

choices.text: One signed by a different key
choices.why: Right. And so does one changed after signing.

choices.text: One pulled by tag instead of digest
choices.why: The tag resolves to a digest, which is what is checked.
